source.name: Who publishes Phi?
source.instructions: In the model catalog, search for **Phi-4** and open its model card. Which company publishes the Phi family of small language models?
source.guidance: Every model card lists its publisher near the model name. Phi is Microsoft's family of small language models (SLMs) — small enough to run cheaply, still strong at reasoning tasks.

source.name: Who publishes Llama?
source.instructions: Now search the catalog for **Llama** models. Which company publishes the Llama family?
source.guidance: The Llama collection in the catalog is published by Meta. Notice that the catalog brings together models from many companies, not just Microsoft and OpenAI.

answers.answer: Converts text into numeric vectors that can be used for search and similarity comparisons
Holds conversations and answers questions in natural language
Transcribes spoken audio into written text

source.name: What does an embeddings model do?
source.instructions: Search the catalog for **text-embedding-3-small** and open its model card. Based on the card, what does this model do?
source.guidance: The card lists its inference task as *embeddings*: turning text into vectors (long lists of numbers) so that similar meanings end up numerically close together — the foundation of semantic search and RAG. Notice you can also filter the whole catalog by inference task.

source.name: Pick a model: speech to text
source.instructions: Your team needs to **transcribe recorded customer phone calls into text**. Use the catalog's search or task filters to find the model designed for this. Which one is it?
source.guidance: Whisper's model card lists speech recognition / audio transcription as its task. Filtering the catalog by task (e.g. *speech*) is the fastest way to answer "which model should I use for X?" questions.

source.name: Pick a model: image generation
source.instructions: A marketing team wants to **generate product images from text descriptions**. Which model from the catalog fits that job?
source.guidance: DALL·E 3 is a text-to-image model. Phi-4 and Mistral Large are text (chat completion) models, and Whisper is speech-to-text — the catalog's task labels tell you this at a glance.

source.name: Who's in the catalog?
source.instructions: Browse the catalog's **collections / publisher filter**. Which of the following actually publish models in the Azure AI Foundry model catalog? *(Select all that apply.)*
source.guidance: Microsoft, Meta, and Mistral AI all have collections in the catalog (along with OpenAI, Cohere, and others). "Fabrikam" is a fictional company Microsoft uses in documentation examples — you won't find it publishing models!

answers.answer: Managed compute — you reserve and pay for dedicated virtual machines
Downloading the model weights and running them on your laptop
Printing the model card and mailing it to Microsoft

source.name: Deployment options
source.instructions: Open any large chat model's card (for example **GPT-4o mini** or **Mistral Large**) and look at its **deployment options**. Which option means *Microsoft hosts the model for you and you pay per use, without managing any servers*?
source.guidance: With serverless (standard / pay-as-you-go) deployments you just call an API and pay per token — Microsoft runs the infrastructure. Managed compute gives you dedicated VMs for models that need them (more control, more cost). Model cards list which options each model supports.

source.name: Challenge 1 — Coach the assistant
source.instructions:
Write and grade your **system prompt** for Bluff City Bikes in the Prompt Lab until it scores **70 or higher**, then click **CHECK IT** to record your grade.

If you haven't passed yet, this check prints the grader's suggestions — refine your prompt in the Prompt Lab and try again. There is no attempt limit.
source.guidance: Your grade comes from the Prompt Lab's rubric: role & persona, scope & guardrails, tone, and output rules.

source.name: Challenge 2 — Sharpen the ask
source.instructions:
Rewrite the vague recycling request as a strong **user prompt** in the Prompt Lab until it scores **70 or higher**, then click **CHECK IT** to record your grade.

If you haven't passed yet, this check prints the grader's suggestions — refine and re-run. There is no attempt limit.
source.guidance: The rubric rewards context & purpose, one clear task, format & length constraints, and quality cues.

source.name: Challenge 3 — Structured output
source.instructions:
Write the **system + user prompts** that make the model return clean JSON in the Prompt Lab until they score **70 or higher**, then click **CHECK IT** to record your grade.

There is no attempt limit.
source.guidance: Watch the automatic format check under your results: the reply must be valid JSON with exactly the five required keys and nothing else around it. If a markdown fence (```) keeps appearing, forbid it explicitly in your system prompt.
